fc-1.definition: The throughput limitation caused by the shared single physical bus connecting the CPU to memory, which forces instructions and data to be transferred sequentially.
fc-1.example: Modern architectures mitigate this using multi-level cache hierarchies (L1, L2, L3) and separate instruction/data caches.

fc-2.definition: A dedicated software routine executed by the operating system when a hardware or software interrupt occurs, handling the trigger before resuming previous execution.
fc-2.example: When a key is pressed, the keyboard controller triggers an interrupt line and the OS dispatches the keyboard ISR.

fc-3.definition: A specialized electronic circuit composed of thousands of parallel execution cores optimized for performing simultaneous repetitive floating-point matrix calculations.
fc-3.example: Used for accelerating matrix multiplications in deep learning and 3D graphic rendering pipelines.

fc-4.definition: A transmission paradigm where data streams are split into independent packets routed dynamically across intermediary nodes based on optimal routing metrics.
fc-4.example: Contrasted with circuit switching where a dedicated physical communication path is occupied for the entire call.

fc-5.definition: A cryptographic protocol that provides end-to-end communications security over a computer network using asymmetric public key cryptography for handshakes and symmetric encryption for session payloads.
fc-5.example: Provides encryption, integrity checks, and authentication for HTTPS web traffic.

fc-6.definition: A database schema design standard where all relations are in 2NF and no non-prime attribute is transitively dependent on any candidate key.
fc-6.example: 'Every non-key attribute must depend on the key, the whole key, and nothing but the key, so help me Codd.'

fc-7.definition: A relational constraint requiring that every foreign key value in a child table must match an existing primary key value in the referenced parent table or be NULL.
fc-7.example: Enforced with 'ON DELETE CASCADE' or 'ON DELETE RESTRICT' constraints in SQL.

fc-8.definition: An error scenario where an ML model learns the random noise and idiosyncrasies of its training set rather than the underlying pattern, degrading performance on unseen test data.
fc-8.example: Mitigated by regularization, dropout layers, early stopping, and data augmentation.

fc-9.definition: Systematic and repeatable errors in a computer system that generate unfair outcomes, often stemming from skewed or unrepresentative training data or flawed modeling assumptions.
fc-9.example: Facial recognition models performing with higher error rates on underrepresented demographic groups.

fc-10.definition: The breakdown of a complex problem, system, or algorithm into smaller, self-contained, and more manageable constituent components.
fc-10.example: Decomposing an e-commerce platform into catalog, shopping cart, authentication, and payment gateway modules.

fc-11.definition: An efficient search algorithm that finds the position of a target value within a sorted list by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half with O(log n) time complexity.
fc-11.example: Searching a sorted list of 1,000,000 items takes at most 20 comparisons.

fc-12.definition: A mathematical notation that describes the limiting behavior of an algorithm's execution time as the input size n grows towards infinity.
fc-12.example: Linear search is O(n), Bubble Sort is O(n²), and Merge Sort is O(n log n).

fc-13.definition: The bundling of data attributes and the methods that operate on that data into a single unit (class), while restricting direct access to internal components.
fc-13.example: Using private attributes (`__balance`) with public accessor methods (`deposit`, `withdraw`).

fc-14.definition: The ability of different object classes to respond to the same method call in distinct, class-specific ways through method overriding.
fc-14.example: A base class `Shape` defines `draw()`; subclasses `Circle` and `Square` implement custom `draw()` routines.

fc-15.definition: A linear data structure operating under the First-In-First-Out rule, where new elements are enqueued at the rear and elements are dequeued from the front.
fc-15.example: Printer spool queues and OS process ready queues.

fc-16.definition: A linear collection of elements with two principal operations: push (adds to top) and pop (removes from top), following the Last-In-First-Out discipline.
fc-16.example: Used in the call stack for managing function execution and recursion frames.

fc-cs-1.definition: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model: A generative deep learning framework that models data generation as the reverse of a progressive Gaussian noise injection Markov chain.
fc-cs-1.example: Visionary Studios art directors use DDPM to synthesize initial photorealistic campaign concepts from pure Gaussian noise.

fc-cs-2.definition: A class of generative models that learns to recover target data by estimating and subtracting injected noise across parameterized discrete timesteps.
fc-cs-2.example: Used for high-fidelity text-to-image synthesis by iteratively denoising Gaussian noise tensors over T=1000 timesteps.

fc-cs-3.definition: The deliberate, scheduled addition of Gaussian noise to an image tensor over timesteps t during the forward diffusion process.
fc-cs-3.example: At timestep T=1000 in the variance schedule βt, the original graphic x0 is transformed into isotropic Gaussian noise.

fc-cs-4.definition: The algorithmic estimation and removal of injected noise from a corrupted input representation, performed by a parameterized neural network (typically a U-Net).
fc-cs-4.example: The U-Net predicts the exact noise vector εθ added at timestep t, subtracting it from xt to recover xt-1.

fc-cs-5.definition: Image generation guided by explicit external constraints, such as natural language text prompts, class category labels, segmentation depth maps, or edge sketches.
fc-cs-5.example: Conditioning synthesis on 'luxury watch in minimalist marble studio' via cross-attention token embeddings.

fc-cs-6.definition: Generating novel samples purely from learned data distribution statistics without any external guiding prompts or class conditions.
fc-cs-6.example: Sampling randomly from isotropic Gaussian noise to generate diverse unguided landscape visuals.

fc-cs-7.definition: Synthesizing coherent spatial imagery conditioned on textual descriptions using multimodal semantic cross-attention embeddings (e.g. CLIP).
fc-cs-7.example: Translating natural language advertising copy into high-fidelity concept storyboard assets for Visionary Studios.

fc-cs-8.definition: Transforming an existing source visual representation into a target artistic style or domain while preserving underlying spatial geometry.
fc-cs-8.example: Converting rough client hand-sketched wireframes into photorealistic rendered product mockups.

fc-cs-9.definition: Mapping discrete words or visual patches into a continuous, dense, semantic vector space where distance corresponds to contextual conceptual similarity.
fc-cs-9.example: A CLIP text encoder converts prompt tokens into 768-dimensional normalized directional vectors.

fc-cs-10.definition: Systematically filtering, balancing, deduplicating, and auditing training data to ensure copyright compliance, artist permission, and representational fairness.
fc-cs-10.example: Visionary Studios audits image corpora to remove scraped uncredited artist portfolios and prevent IP infringement.

fc-cs-11.definition: Active algorithmic and statistical measures designed to identify and eliminate systematic skew, prejudice, or demographic stereotyping in AI generation.
fc-cs-11.example: Balancing training sets across demographic and cultural axes so generated professional roles avoid historical societal skew.

fc-cs-12.definition: Preserving identical facial identity, attire, proportions, and lighting of a subject across multiple distinct generated camera angles and scenes.
fc-cs-12.example: Using identity embeddings or LoRA adaptations to keep the same brand ambassador consistent across a multi-ad rollout.

fc-cs-13.definition: Convolutional Neural Network: A specialized deep architecture using spatial kernels with translation invariance, widely utilized in computer vision and GAN discriminators.
fc-cs-13.example: Feature extraction layers in the Inception-v3 classifier used to extract deep perceptual feature maps for FID calculations.

fc-cs-14.definition: Generative Adversarial Network: A two-player zero-sum minimax framework where a Generator and Discriminator compete against each other to produce synthetic outputs.
fc-cs-14.example: Using an adversarial discriminator patch loss to force super-resolution upscalers to produce photorealistic fine micro-textures.

fc-cs-15.definition: The two competing networks in a GAN: the Generator synthesizes fake samples from random noise, while the Discriminator acts as a binary classifier discerning real from fake.
fc-cs-15.example: Generator minimizes log(1 - D(G(z))) while Discriminator maximizes log D(x) + log(1 - D(G(z))).

fc-cs-16.definition: The continuous competitive optimization dynamic between Generator and Discriminator, converging toward a Nash equilibrium where the discriminator cannot distinguish authentic from synthetic data.
fc-cs-16.example: Both networks improve simultaneously until discriminator accuracy hovers at random guessing (D(x) = 0.5).

fc-cs-17.definition: A severe failure mode in GAN training where the Generator outputs only a narrow subset of realistic images that fools the Discriminator, ignoring the variety of the true dataset distribution.
fc-cs-17.example: Synthesizing only one specific car angle repeatedly across all vehicle prompts, destroying advertising campaign diversity.

fc-cs-18.definition: A compressed, lower-dimensional manifold representation where high-dimensional data (e.g. 1024x1024 images) is compactly encoded while retaining core perceptual semantics.
fc-cs-18.example: Compressing an image from 1024x1024x3 down to a 128x128x4 latent tensor to execute diffusion with 64x less computation.

fc-cs-19.definition: Variational Autoencoder: A probabilistic generative architecture that encodes input data into a parameterized latent Gaussian distribution and reconstructs it via a decoder.
fc-cs-19.example: The VAE encoder strips imperceptible high-frequency pixel noise before latent diffusion, while the decoder reconstructs crisp pixels.

fc-cs-20.definition: An architectural fusion combining distinct generative approaches (such as VAE perceptual compression + latent diffusion + GAN perceptual patch loss) to maximize fidelity while minimizing compute.
fc-cs-20.example: Latent Diffusion Models (LDM) marry VAE compression with U-Net score-based denoising to achieve fast, high-DPI generation.

fc-cs-21.definition: An exact-likelihood generative architecture utilizing invertible transformations with tractable Jacobian determinants to map directly between data and latent spaces.
fc-cs-21.example: Provides exact log-likelihood calculation and bijective mapping between pixel space and latent vectors without approximation.

fc-cs-22.definition: Fréchet Inception Distance: The gold standard metric evaluating synthetic imagery by calculating the Wasserstein-2 distance between Gaussian feature distributions of real and fake images in deep feature space. Lower is better.
fc-cs-22.example: Visionary Studios measures FID against client reference photos; lower scores confirm high visual fidelity and diverse outputs.

fc-cs-23.definition: An early generative metric measuring conditional class confidence (sharpness) and marginal distribution entropy (diversity) on synthetic images alone, without reference to real images. Higher is better.
fc-cs-23.example: Unable to detect mode collapse when generated outputs are sharp, making it inferior to FID for commercial quality assurance.
